events.text: Case opened: The Nightingale Vanishes

On Thursday at 21:40, insurance appraiser Odile Marchetti examined the Ravel Gallery's prize piece — the Nightingale, a nineteenth-century jewelled clockwork bird insured for 3.5 million — in the gallery's vault and declared it a replica. The real bird is gone. The vault was locked all week and nobody reported a break-in. In the previous ten days the bird had been out for restoration and returned on Monday night; the vault was also opened in the small hours of Wednesday. Gallery owner Lucien Ravel recently raised the insurance cover. Restorer Irene Vance had the bird in her studio. Security consultant Felix Dorn built the vault system. Find out when the switch happened, who made it, and whether anyone should be charged.
Set out how I intend to run this.

Somebody in that building is behind the theft of the Ravel Nightingale, and I've got three names: Lucien Ravel, Irene Vance, Felix Dorn. I'll walk the scene, then I want them in a room one at a time while their stories are still warm. People crack before paperwork does.
Flag the easy assumption.

The fake is my best witness. Every replica carries the hand of whoever made it — the enamel, the tool marks, the casting seams. Get me the bird, the case, every log that touched that vault, and I will tell you who could have made it.
Tell the team what a charge needs.
Bring me a story a jury can feel: who wanted that bird and could reach it, who was close enough to do it, and one exhibit I can hold up in closing. Get me that and I'll do the rest.

events.text: Irene Vance switched the Nightingale on Monday night, not Wednesday. Insolvent and owed two years of fees by Lucien Ravel, she spent the ten days of the restoration casting a replica from a silicone mould. On Monday she asked the night guard to pause the corridor camera 'for her photographs', put the fake in the display case at 23:09, and walked out of the loading door with the real bird in her equipment case. On Tuesday morning she shipped it to a dealer in Antwerp as 'restoration materials' declared at 900,000. The vault opening on Wednesday night that looked like the theft was Felix Dorn secretly replacing a faulty sensor; the owner with the debts and the raised insurance was at a card table across town.

data.motive: Insolvency, and two years of unpaid fees from the gallery — settled with a 900,000 private sale.
data.method: A replica cast during the restoration and swapped in when she returned the bird, with the corridor camera paused at her request.

detective.name: Det. Ada Marlowe
detective.tagline: Gets a feeling about someone and will not let go.
detective.personality: Instinctive, fast, confrontational. Picks a suspect early and squeezes. Brilliant when right, stubborn when wrong.
detective.background: Ex-vice. Believes most cases are solved in the interview room, not the lab.

forensic.name: Dr. Freja Lindqvist
forensic.tagline: Finds the story inside the sample.
forensic.personality: Enthusiastic, vivid, loves a good reconstruction. Occasionally needs reining in.
forensic.background: Came to forensics from materials science.

prosecutor.name: Prosecutor Dex Harlan
prosecutor.tagline: Never met a jury he could not move.
prosecutor.personality: Theatrical, aggressive, loves a narrative. Sometimes reaches further than the exhibits allow.
prosecutor.background: Former actor. Wins big, and occasionally loses big.

defense.name: Barnaby Finch, Esq.
defense.tagline: Objects first, thinks later, wins anyway.
defense.personality: Combative, quick on his feet, objects often. Loves an alternative suspect.
defense.background: Thirty years of jury trials and one unfortunate contempt citation.

judge.name: Hon. Otis Brannigan
judge.tagline: Runs a tight courtroom and a dry wit.
judge.personality: Impatient with theatrics, generous with latitude on cross. Occasionally sardonic.

lucien.name: Cornelius Blythe
lucien.tagline: Could sell you your own watch.
lucien.personality: A domineering performer: charming, evasive, counter-attacks when cornered.

irene.name: Selene Voss-Hart
irene.tagline: Disappears into whoever she is asked to be.
irene.personality: A guarded performer: gives exactly what the question requires. Holds a cover story under pressure until the evidence makes it untenable.

felix.name: Pip Abernathy
felix.personality: A nervous performer: over-explains, backtracks, cracks early when confronted with records.

pavel.name: Dolores Mbeki
pavel.personality: A plain-spoken performer: cooperative, proud, defensive about her own conduct.

odile.name: Milo Tran
odile.personality: A chatty performer: digresses, gossips, enjoys attention; gives up awkward details when pressed gently.

juror1.name: Agnes Whitlock
juror1.tagline: Retired auditor. Wants it in writing.
juror1.personality: Needs every element proved. Unmoved by rhetoric; counts exhibits.

juror2.name: Walt Kowalski
juror2.tagline: Retired machinist. Thinks they usually did it.
juror2.personality: Inclined to trust the police, but stubbornly honest about a hole in the story.

juror3.name: Priya Raman
